title: When neighbours go wrong
titleChinese: 造成邻里不和的种种因素
paragraphs: Do you know the names of the people who live next door? Chances are you live next to someone, but do you actually know them? Sadly, the only time we do seem to hear about people’s neighbours is when things go wrong – hearing people say things like they have the neighbours from hell! So, what does go wrong?

When talking about famous feuds with people who live in proximity, you only need to think of the Montagues and Capulets in Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet. Thankfully, most real-life quarrels don’t go that far. These days, especially in cities, many people live in condominiums, tightly packed into apartment blocks. Our neighbours are all around us – so what issues can come from that?

The first obvious cause of dispute is noise pollution. Loud bass pumping through the walls, construction, or people arguing next door can disrupt the harmony of your living space. Asking someone directly to turn the music down can cause you to feel anxious. However, getting someone like a building manager involved to speak to your neighbour and making complaints official can make things more awkward down the line as you didn’t speak to your neighbour directly.

And then what about smells? If your neighbour likes eating especially pungent food, something that offends your nostrils, and that smell drifts through your window, what can you do? Some other common issues include water leaking through the ceiling, pets making noise, and littering from the balcony above you.

And then, if you’re lucky enough to own a garden, that can present even more issues to fight with your neighbour about! This could include hedges and fences that are too high, balls and toys invading your garden or hitting your windows, and boundary disputes over where your neighbours’ land ends. All these can create animosity over time.

It’s not easy living next door to someone, especially if they’re noisy. But having a clear and honest line of dialogue might help. Also, try considering if the things you are doing could upset your neighbours. If it’s something that would upset you, maybe think again.

vocabulary.entry: neighbours from hell /ˈneɪbəz frəm hel/ （口语）地狱邻居；令人头疼的邻居
vocabulary.example: She moved out quickly because she had neighbours from hell who partied every night.
vocabulary.translation: 她很快就搬走了，因为她的邻居特别糟心，每晚都开派对。

vocabulary.entry: feud /fjuːd/ n. 长期不和；世仇
vocabulary.example: The two families have been in a feud for over a hundred years.
vocabulary.translation: 这两大家族的世仇已经持续了一百多年。

vocabulary.entry: in proximity /ɪn prɒkˈsɪməti/ 在附近；邻近
vocabulary.example: The new hospital was built in proximity to the residential area.
vocabulary.translation: 这家新医院建在了居民区附近。

vocabulary.entry: quarrel /ˈkwɒrəl/ n. 争吵；口角
vocabulary.example: The trivial matter led to a bitter quarrel between the two friends.
vocabulary.translation: 这件小事引发了两个朋友之间激烈的争吵。

vocabulary.entry: condominium /ˌkɒndəˈmɪniəm/ n. 公寓大楼；共管公寓
vocabulary.example: He bought a spacious apartment in a new condominium downtown.
vocabulary.translation: 他在市中心一栋新建的公寓大楼里买了一套宽敞的公寓。

vocabulary.entry: tightly packed /ˈtaɪtli pækt/ 拥挤的；紧密排列的
vocabulary.example: The tightly packed audience filled every seat in the theatre.
vocabulary.translation: 拥挤的观众坐满了剧院里的每一个座位。

vocabulary.entry: apartment block /əˈpɑːtmənt blɒk/ 公寓楼
vocabulary.example: They live on the fifth floor of a modern apartment block.
vocabulary.translation: 他们住在一栋现代化公寓楼的五楼。

vocabulary.entry: dispute /dɪˈspjuːt/ n. 争端；争执
vocabulary.example: The two countries held talks to resolve the border dispute.
vocabulary.translation: 两国举行会谈，以解决边境争端。

vocabulary.entry: noise pollution /nɔɪz pəˈluːʃn/ 噪音污染
vocabulary.example: The government has introduced laws to control noise pollution in cities.
vocabulary.translation: 政府出台了相关法律来控制城市里的噪音污染。

vocabulary.entry: loud bass /laʊd beɪs/ 重低音
vocabulary.example: The loud bass from the party next door kept me awake all night.
vocabulary.translation: 隔壁派对的重低音吵得我整夜没睡。

vocabulary.entry: disrupt harmony /dɪsˈrʌpt ˈhɑːməni/ 破坏和谐
vocabulary.example: The constant arguments between the couple disrupted the harmony of the neighbourhood.
vocabulary.translation: 这对夫妻频繁的争吵破坏了邻里间的和谐。

vocabulary.entry: building manager /ˈbɪldɪŋ ˈmænɪdʒə(r)/ 物业经理；大楼管理员
vocabulary.example: I reported the broken lift to the building manager this morning.
vocabulary.translation: 今天早上我向物业经理报修了故障电梯。

vocabulary.entry: pungent /ˈpʌndʒənt/ adj. 气味刺鼻的；辛辣的
vocabulary.example: The pungent smell of garlic filled the kitchen.
vocabulary.translation: 厨房里弥漫着大蒜刺鼻的气味。

vocabulary.entry: offend nostrils /əˈfend ˈnɒstrɪlz/ 刺鼻；让鼻子不适
vocabulary.example: The smell of rotten eggs offended our nostrils as we walked past the bin.
vocabulary.translation: 我们路过垃圾桶时，腐烂鸡蛋的气味刺鼻难忍。

vocabulary.entry: water leaking /ˈwɔːtə ˈliːkɪŋ/ 漏水
vocabulary.example: Water leaking from the ceiling damaged the carpet in the living room.
vocabulary.translation: 天花板漏水损坏了客厅的地毯。

vocabulary.entry: littering /ˈlɪtərɪŋ/ n. 乱扔垃圾
vocabulary.example: Littering in public places is punishable by fine in this city.
vocabulary.translation: 在这座城市，公共场所乱扔垃圾会被处以罚款。

vocabulary.entry: balcony /ˈbælkəni/ n. 阳台
vocabulary.example: She likes to sit on the balcony and read books on sunny afternoons.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢在晴朗的午后坐在阳台上看书。

vocabulary.entry: hedge /hedʒ/ n. 树篱；绿篱
vocabulary.example: The gardener trimmed the hedge to keep it neat and tidy.
vocabulary.translation: 园丁修剪了树篱，让它保持整齐美观。

vocabulary.entry: fence /fens/ n. 栅栏；篱笆
vocabulary.example: They built a wooden fence around the garden to keep the dog inside.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在花园周围建了一道木栅栏，防止狗跑出去。

vocabulary.entry: boundary dispute /ˈbaʊndri dɪˈspjuːt/ 边界纠纷
vocabulary.example: The boundary dispute between the two farmers was settled by a local official.
vocabulary.translation: 当地官员调解解决了两位农民之间的边界纠纷。

vocabulary.entry: animosity /ˌænɪˈmɒsəti/ n. 敌意；怨恨
vocabulary.example: Years of argument have created a lot of animosity between the two families.
vocabulary.translation: 多年的争吵让两家人之间积怨颇深。

vocabulary.entry: line of dialogue /laɪn əv ˈdaɪəlɒɡ/ 沟通渠道；对话途径
vocabulary.example: Establishing a clear line of dialogue is key to solving the problem.
vocabulary.translation: 建立清晰的沟通渠道是解决这个问题的关键。

vocabulary.entry: invade /ɪnˈveɪd/ v. 侵入；闯入
vocabulary.example: The children's balls often invade our garden from the next door.
vocabulary.translation: 邻居家孩子的球经常会滚进我们的花园。

vocabulary.entry: construction /kənˈstrʌkʃn/ n. 建筑施工
vocabulary.example: The construction outside the window made it hard to concentrate on work.
vocabulary.translation: 窗外的建筑施工噪音让人难以专心工作。

vocabulary.entry: official complaint /əˈfɪʃl kəmˈpleɪnt/ 正式投诉
vocabulary.example: He filed an official complaint with the property management about the noise issue.
vocabulary.translation: 他就噪音问题向物业提交了正式投诉。

sentences.english: Do you know the names of the people who live next door?
sentences.chinese: 你知道隔壁邻居的名字吗？

sentences.english: Chances are you live next to someone, but do you actually know them?
sentences.chinese: 你大概率有邻居，但你真的了解他们吗？

sentences.english: Sadly, the only time we do seem to hear about people’s neighbours is when things go wrong – hearing people say things like they have the neighbours from hell!
sentences.chinese: 遗憾的是，我们似乎只有在邻里关系出问题的时候，才会听到人们谈论邻居——比如常听到有人抱怨自己遇上了“极品邻居”！

sentences.english: So, what does go wrong?
sentences.chinese: 那么，究竟是哪些问题会引发邻里矛盾呢？

sentences.english: When talking about famous feuds with people who live in proximity, you only need to think of the Montagues and Capulets in Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet.
sentences.chinese: 说到著名的邻里宿怨，你只需要想想莎士比亚《罗密欧与朱丽叶》中的蒙太古家族和凯普莱特家族就够了。

sentences.english: Thankfully, most real-life quarrels don’t go that far.
sentences.chinese: 幸好，现实生活中的大多数邻里争吵都不会闹到那么过分。

sentences.english: These days, especially in cities, many people live in condominiums, tightly packed into apartment blocks.
sentences.chinese: 如今，尤其是在城市里，许多人住在格局紧凑的公寓楼里。

sentences.english: Our neighbours are all around us – so what issues can come from that?
sentences.chinese: 邻居们近在咫尺——那么，这种居住环境会引发哪些问题呢？

sentences.english: The first obvious cause of dispute is noise pollution.
sentences.chinese: 引发邻里纠纷的第一个显而易见的原因是噪音污染。

sentences.english: Loud bass pumping through the walls, construction, or people arguing next door can disrupt the harmony of your living space.
sentences.chinese: 穿墙而来的强劲低音、施工的嘈杂声、或是隔壁邻居的争吵声，都可能破坏你居住空间的和谐氛围。

sentences.english: Asking someone directly to turn the music down can cause you to feel anxious.
sentences.chinese: 直接要求对方把音乐声调小，可能会让你感到紧张不安。

sentences.english: However, getting someone like a building manager involved to speak to your neighbour and making complaints official can make things more awkward down the line as you didn’t speak to your neighbour directly.
sentences.chinese: 但如果让物业经理这类人出面沟通，或是正式投诉，又会因为你没有直接和邻居交涉，而让后续的邻里相处变得更加尴尬。

sentences.english: And then what about smells?
sentences.chinese: 还有气味问题。

sentences.english: If your neighbour likes eating especially pungent food, something that offends your nostrils, and that smell drifts through your window, what can you do?
sentences.chinese: 如果你的邻居喜欢吃气味特别浓烈、让你难以忍受的食物，而且这些味道飘进了你的窗户，你该怎么办？

sentences.english: Some other common issues include water leaking through the ceiling, pets making noise, and littering from the balcony above you.
sentences.chinese: 其他常见的邻里问题还包括天花板漏水、宠物吵闹、以及楼上邻居从阳台往下乱扔垃圾。

sentences.english: And then, if you’re lucky enough to own a garden, that can present even more issues to fight with your neighbour about!
sentences.chinese: 如果你足够幸运，拥有一片自家花园，那可能会引发更多和邻居争吵的问题！

sentences.english: This could include hedges and fences that are too high, balls and toys invading your garden or hitting your windows, and boundary disputes over where your neighbours’ land ends.
sentences.chinese: 比如邻居家的树篱或围栏过高、球和玩具掉进你家花园甚至砸到窗户、以及关于邻里地界划分的纠纷。

sentences.english: All these can create animosity over time.
sentences.chinese: 久而久之，这些问题都会滋生邻里间的敌意。

sentences.english: It’s not easy living next door to someone, especially if they’re noisy.
sentences.chinese: 和别人做邻居并非易事，尤其是当对方很吵闹的时候。

sentences.english: But having a clear and honest line of dialogue might help.
sentences.chinese: 但保持清晰坦诚的沟通或许能起到作用。

sentences.english: Also, try considering if the things you are doing could upset your neighbours.
sentences.chinese: 此外，不妨换位思考一下，自己的所作所为是否会打扰到邻居。

sentences.english: If it’s something that would upset you, maybe think again.
sentences.chinese: 如果换作是你，也会为此感到不快，那或许就该三思而后行了。
